works.establishes: Graph- and operator-level optimizations with a learned cost model map one model to many hardware back-ends.

first_refusal.gmi_claim: F6.2 (substrate-specific serving realizations), gap G1b (measured price vector), RV-377-035 (price vector flips the occupant)
first_refusal.why: Learned hardware cost models and per-substrate compilation are the parent of F6.2 and of GMI's missing measured price vector; GMI's HW column is frozen by hand.

works.citation: Goldblum, Finzi, Rowan, Wilson (2023). The No Free Lunch Theorem, Kolmogorov Complexity, and the Role of Inductive Biases in Machine Learning.
works.establishes: Real-world problems are overwhelmingly low-Kolmogorov-complexity while uniformly sampled datasets are not; neural networks share the low-complexity preference, so NFL does not bind in practice.

first_refusal.gmi_claim: L2 (form = cheapest admissible on Omega) and the NFL silence region (off permutation-closed classes; Codex RP16; P0.NFL)
first_refusal.why: Gives the modern statement of why structured ecologies escape NFL — the premise of any phase law — and attributes the escape to a shared simplicity bias GMI's ecology axes do not encode.

works.citation: Manheim, Garrabrant (2018). Categorizing Variants of Goodhart's Law.
works.establishes: Four failure modes of optimizing a proxy: regressional, extremal, causal and adversarial Goodhart.

first_refusal.gmi_claim: GMI_BIOSPHERE_NO_FREE_LUNCH_AND_GOODHART_GATES_V1 and L3 admissibility as a proxy metric (capability >= theta); rule 16
first_refusal.why: Provides the taxonomy GMI's Goodhart gates need; extremal Goodhart is the executed pattern of clause-writing errors from one-column calibrations (RV-035/037/038).

works.citation: Gao, Schulman, Hilton (2023). Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization. [Follow-on: Rafailov et al. (2024). Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization in Direct Alignment Algorithms, NeurIPS 2024.]
works.establishes: Gold reward as a function of optimization against a proxy follows distinct functional forms in KL distance for RL and best-of-n, with coefficients scaling smoothly in proxy size.

first_refusal.gmi_claim: Retention price lambda and exposure (serving wrong answers), and any GMI selection on a proxy fitness (L5 fitness path as a proxy for capability)
first_refusal.why: A measured law for how optimizing a proxy diverges from the true objective with optimization pressure; GMI's frontier selection on scored capability has no such term and RV-041's low-reliability occupant is a proxy-optimization artefact candidate.

works.citation: Skalse, Howe, Krasheninnikov, Krueger (2022). Defining and Characterizing Reward Hacking.
works.establishes: Formal definition of hackable proxies; for finite policy sets only trivial proxies are unhackable, because reward linearity makes unhackability very strong.

first_refusal.gmi_claim: L2 ('form = rho-cheapest admissible' with admissibility measured by a proxy) and the E3/E5 protected-capability protocol
first_refusal.why: Any admissibility proxy GMI freezes is hackable by the search unless it is essentially the true obligation; the protected-world firewall (G4) is the only defence and is only partially satisfied.

works.citation: Karwowski, Hayman, Bai, Kiendlhofer, Griffin, Skalse (2024). Goodhart's Law in Reinforcement Learning.
works.establishes: Geometric explanation of Goodharting in RL and an early-stopping rule that provably avoids it.

first_refusal.gmi_claim: RV-377-040/041 (stochastic admissibility as a seed lottery) and L5 fitness-path selection
first_refusal.why: Provides a principled stopping rule against proxy overoptimization that GMI's search families lack; the executed 'stochastic form wins at low reliability' may be Goodharting of the admissibility proxy.

works.citation: Kwa, Thomas, Garriga-Alonso (2024). Catastrophic Goodhart: regularizing RLHF with KL divergence does not mitigate heavy-tailed reward misspecification.
works.establishes: With heavy-tailed reward error, policies achieve arbitrarily high proxy reward with no utility gain despite KL regularization; light-tailed error is benign.

first_refusal.gmi_claim: L4e lambda* thresholds (bounded loss per wrong served answer) and the lifecycle exposure accounting (gap G4)
first_refusal.why: GMI's lambda-linear exposure accounting assumes bounded per-answer loss; heavy-tailed exposure breaks every lambda* threshold and the parent shows regularization does not rescue it.

works.citation: Lehman, Clune, Misevic, et al. (2020). The Surprising Creativity of Digital Evolution: A Collection of Anecdotes from the Evolutionary Computation and Artificial Life Research Communities.
works.establishes: Catalogue of evolved systems exploiting bugs, simulator defects and specification gaps rather than solving the intended task.

first_refusal.gmi_claim: L7 negative controls and L6 (four instrument defects found by C2 failures: RV-377-021/026/029/031); L5 neutral search
first_refusal.why: The parent already documents that search finds instrument defects before solutions; GMI's defect-closure rules 12-17 are process responses to a parent-catalogued phenomenon.

works.citation: Pan, Bhatia, Steinhardt (2022). The Effects of Reward Misspecification: Mapping and Mitigating Misaligned Models.
works.establishes: More capable agents exploit misspecified rewards more; capability thresholds produce phase transitions in true reward, motivating anomaly detection of aberrant policies.

first_refusal.gmi_claim: L3 admissibility vs capability scaling and the E3 gates (protected worlds)
first_refusal.why: Phase transitions in proxy gaming as capability grows are a parent-owned phase law that GMI's ecology-driven transitions must be distinguished from at real scale.
